title: Stillwater Lane street systems
note: Every part carries its own `metres`, because the group anchor alone put the manhole at 2.5 m across and the bollard at 1.56 m — see the per-object scale note in author-prop-group.py. Sizes below are real Japanese street dimensions, and each is solved from the axis that the scene actually has to fit: height for anything a person stands beside, footprint for anything set into the ground.

parts.label: Traffic signal pole with mast arm
Wall-mounted street lamp on mounting pier
parts.note: Arrives with the pier it was drawn against. Kept rather than cropped — doc 21 §2 puts wall-mounted utility along the boundary wall, and the pier buries into a wall face at placement.

parts.label: Painted steel pedestrian guard rail
parts.note: Solved from height, not length: 1.1 m is doc 21 §4's rail band and is the dimension read at human scale. Length follows at ~1.6 m and the run is built by repeating the panel.

parts.label: Cast iron drain grates in concrete pad
parts.note: Solved from footprint. A ground-set object is fitted to the paving, and its thickness is a consequence rather than a target.

parts.label: Cast iron manhole cover in concrete pad
Standpipe with valve wheel on plinth

lodNote: LOD0 is deliberately NOT decimated. Section 8's 20k-180k props band was written for HERO props; a 0.9 m bollard and a 0.6 m manhole cover are supporting street furniture and arrive at 7k-47k once the group's 152,954 triangles are divided across eight objects. Decimating them further to hit a floor written for something else would throw away silhouette for nothing. The set TOTAL is 152,954 at LOD0, which is one hero prop's worth of triangles for eight placeable objects — reported plainly rather than dressed as a band pass.
slotNote: Slot indices are into the 17 `model_segment` material slots, sorted along rowAxis. Declared rather than inferred: automatic largest-gap regrouping handed the traffic signal head and mast arm to the wall lamp, because the arm reaches sideways and its slot centroid sat nearer the lamp's than its own pole's. Verified against launch-plan/review/captures/props/PROP-LANE-01/contact-sheet.png. Slot 4 (the three-aspect signal head) reads as if it belongs to the wall pier because Tripo placed it 1.8 m along the row from the pole — which is where a MAST-ARM head belongs. It is assigned to the signal pole, and the apparent conflict is a row-overlap artefact rather than a partition error.
